verdict.rationale: Snyk's own docs show per-language CLI scanning for Java/Kotlin (Maven and Gradle), JavaScript (including Yarn workspaces via --all-projects), .NET (solution/project files plus snyk code test) and Python. It also covers open-source dependencies, source code, containers and IaC (Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes, ARM). Breadth beyond these four language ecosystems is not shown, so 'all the major languages' is only partly evidenced. Missing for 10: a documented full supported-languages/package-manager list, evidence for other major ecosystems (e.g. Go, Ruby, PHP, Swift, C/C++), independent hands-on corroboration of multi-ecosystem accuracy.

support.subject: As a developer, I can scan projects across all the major languages and package ecosystems my organization uses

citations.quote: To test Maven and Gradle Projects, use the `snyk test` command as follows
`--yarn-workspaces`: For Yarn Workspaces use the `--all-projects` flag to test and monitor your packages
To analyze Open Source libraries, install your dependencies, then run `snyk test`... To perform source code analysis, run `snyk code test` from the root of the Project.
To set the Python version in the CLI, add the following option to `snyk test` or `snyk monitor` with the name of the Python binary
Scan, prioritize, and fix vulnerabilities in your code, open-source dependencies, container images, and cloud configurations.
